title: Development
examples: What is the difference between GNI and HDI?
How can a country improve its development?
Why do some countries develop faster than others?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how we measure development in countries.

items: Development is more than just money.
We use indicators to measure it.
These show different aspects of life.

explain.say: One key indicator is Gross National Income, or GNI.
GNI gives us a measure of the total income available to a country's residents.
Another important measure is the Human Development Index, or HDI.
The HDI looks at three areas: health, education, and standard of living.
A gap exists when there is a big difference between countries' development levels.

faq.a: Indicators like GNI and HDI look at different parts of life. GNI only measures money, but HDI measures more than just money.
asks: What is the difference between GNI and HDI?
Do all indicators measure the same thing?
Why use more than just money for development?

faq.q: What is the best indicator for development?
faq.a: There is no single best indicator for development. Different indicators show different strengths of a country.
asks: Should we only focus on money?

faq.q: How can a country reduce the development gap?
faq.a: Countries can improve by investing in education and healthcare. They can also trade more goods globally.
asks: What helps poorer countries catch up?

faq.a: GNI stands for Gross National Income. It is the total income earned by a country's residents.
asks: Is GNI the same as GDP?

faq.a: The HDI measures three key dimensions: life expectancy, years of schooling, and income levels.
asks: What are the three parts of HDI?
Does HDI include quality of life?

facts: GNI measures the total income received by a country's residents.
The HDI combines health, education, and standard of living into one score.
A development gap shows the difference between rich and poor nations.
Strategies for development often involve improving trade and governance.

quiz.say: A country has high income but poor sanitation. Which indicator might show this gap?
quiz.why: The HDI includes health aspects like sanitation, not just income.

wrong.0: GNI only measures the total money earned, ignoring health.
wrong.1: GDP measures total output, not necessarily the quality of life.
wrong.2: Trade Balance only compares imports and exports.

quiz.say: If a country's GNI is rising quickly, what does this suggest?
quiz.why: Rising GNI means more total income is available to the residents.

wrong.0: High HDI means good health and education, which GNI does not guarantee.
wrong.1: High GNI could mean wealth is only held by a few people.
wrong.2: Income growth does not directly predict population stability.

quiz.say: Which combination of factors is central to the HDI?
quiz.why: The HDI explicitly combines these three dimensions for a holistic view.

wrong.0: This mix is too broad and lacks specific metrics.
wrong.1: These are economic sectors, not the specific indicators used.
wrong.2: These are factors, but not the core measurable components of the HDI.
